note: short · single positive mood
transcript: Today was great, honestly one of the best days in ages. I felt happy and light, like everything was clicking into place.

note: short · single low mood
transcript: Rough morning. Woke up heavy and sad and couldn't really shake it for the first few hours.

note: short · flat affect, numb
transcript: Pretty meh day, just kind of numb and going through the motions. Didn't feel much of anything either way.

note: short · neutral-positive, mild
transcript: I'm alright, not bad really. Got curious about a new podcast and ended up taking notes, which was kind of nice.

note: med · full arc: take → onset → crash → side effect → win
transcript: Took my Concerta 36mg at 8am with breakfast. It kicked in after about 45 minutes and I was firing on all cylinders until lunch. Crashed hard around 3pm, dry mouth all afternoon. Still managed to finish the report, proud of that.

note: med · slow onset then locked in
transcript: Took my Elvanse 50mg around 7:30. Took a while to kick in but by mid-morning I was completely locked in and powered through the whole backlog.

note: med · side effects + hard crash, irritable
transcript: The Vyvanse had me wired and jittery, hands literally shaking by mid-afternoon. Then I crashed around 4 and got pretty irritable with everyone.

note: med · smooth positive day
transcript: Ritalin 10mg this morning and the day just flowed. Felt steady and clear, got through everything without the usual afternoon dip.

note: med · forgot dose, distracted day
transcript: Completely forgot to take my Adderall this morning and only realised at lunch. The whole day was a write-off, couldn't focus on a single thing.

note: med · deliberate skip + reason, foggy
transcript: Skipped my Vyvanse today because my heart was racing yesterday and it scared me a bit. Felt foggy and slow all morning without it.

note: med · timing question, mild anxiety
transcript: I think I took my Concerta late, maybe 10am instead of 8, and now I'm worried I won't sleep tonight. Restless about it all evening.

note: med · prescription change, neutral
transcript: The psychiatrist switched me off Strattera and onto Elvanse starting today. First dose went down fine, no obvious side effects yet.

note: med · stacked side effects, low appetite
transcript: The new dose has me with a dry mouth all day, no appetite at lunch, and a bit of a headache by evening. Functional but not comfortable.

note: med · combo, smoother comedown
transcript: Started the morning with Ritalin and I take my Wellbutrin with it now. The combo seems smoother, less of a hard comedown in the afternoon.

note: sleep · short fragmented sleep, foggy
transcript: Slept maybe 5 hours, tossed and turned all night, kept waking up. Felt foggy and irritable the whole morning because of it.

note: sleep · paradox, long sleep still tired
transcript: Slept a solid nine hours and yet I still feel worn out, which makes no sense. Dragged myself through the morning.

note: sleep · good sleep → energized positive
transcript: Eight hours and woke up before the alarm feeling rested. Went for a run, felt genuinely good and alert the whole day.

note: sleep · couldn't wind down, wired late
transcript: Couldn't fall asleep until 2am, heart pounding, mind racing through tomorrow's list. Felt exhausted but completely wired at the same time.

note: sleep · external disruption, drained
transcript: Barely slept, maybe three hours total because the baby was up all night. I'm completely exhausted and running on fumes today.

note: sleep · early waking + anxiety
transcript: Woke at 4:30 and couldn't get back to sleep, just lay there worrying. By the time the alarm went I already felt defeated.

note: focus · executive dysfunction, can't start
transcript: I knew exactly what I needed to do but I just could not start any of it, sat staring at the screen for an hour. My head was all over the place and I felt restless and useless.

note: focus · paralysis short
transcript: Spent the whole morning opening and closing the same document. Couldn't make myself begin.

note: focus/mood · overwhelm then shutdown
transcript: The inbox was a mountain and I felt completely overwhelmed, so I ended up doing nothing at all and just avoided it the whole day.

note: focus · displacement activity instead of work
transcript: Instead of doing the actual work I reorganised my entire desk, alphabetised the spice rack, and deep-cleaned the kitchen. Productive at everything except the thing that mattered.

note: focus · scattered, half-finished tasks
transcript: Started ten things and finished none of them. Kept jumping between tabs and tasks, my brain wouldn't settle on anything.

note: focus · flow state, locked in
transcript: Got into the zone around 10 and didn't look up until 3. Completely locked in, the code just flowed, easily my most productive stretch in weeks.

note: focus · hyperfocus downside, forgot to eat
transcript: I was so deep into the project I forgot to eat lunch and missed two calls. Great focus but I came out of it shaky and starving.

note: mood/focus · win + great mood
transcript: Absolutely nailed the presentation today, the client signed off on the spot. Felt accomplished and proud walking out of that room.

note: ARC · mood up over the day
transcript: Started the day anxious and flat, almost called in sick. But after lunch something shifted, I got moving and by evening I actually felt good and capable.

note: ARC · energy down over the day
transcript: Morning was brilliant, full of energy, smashed through my to-do list. Then the afternoon hit and I completely crashed, could barely keep my eyes open by 4.

note: ARC · emotional settle after action
transcript: I was panicking about the deadline all morning, stomach in knots. Once I finally sent the email it was like a weight lifted and I could breathe again.

note: ARC · win then late-night spiral
transcript: Had a really productive day, felt on top of everything, and then for no reason at all I spiralled in the evening and ended up doomscrolling till midnight feeling awful.

note: neutral · no emotional signal
transcript: Renewed the car insurance, called the dentist to reschedule, and dropped a parcel at the post office. Nothing else on the calendar this week.

note: neutral · weather + chores, no signal
transcript: Light rain most of the morning then it cleared up by lunch. The bins go out tonight and the recycling is on Thursday this week.

note: neutral · contains 'heavy'/'tired' as traps, no real signal
transcript: The shopping bags were heavy and the queue was tiring, but otherwise just a normal trip to the supermarket. Bought milk, bread, and some batteries.

note: neutral · pure scheduling
transcript: The plumber is booked for nine, the parcel arrives between noon and four, and I've got a call at two-thirty. Busy diary but nothing dramatic.

note: long · stream of consciousness, hedged
transcript: So like I don't really know how to describe today, it was kind of all over the place honestly. Woke up late again, missed the gym which I always feel guilty about, and then spent way too long just scrolling instead of starting work. By the afternoon I sort of pulled it together and actually got through the big task I'd been avoiding for a week, which felt good, but then I was so wired I couldn't wind down and ended up awake till 1am again. Classic.

note: long · introspective, mixed feelings
transcript: Been thinking a lot about whether the meds are actually helping or whether I've just gotten used to them. Some days like today I feel clear and steady and I think yes, definitely, this is working. Other days I wonder if I'm flattening out the parts of me I actually like. Today was a good day though, calm and focused, so I'll take it and not overthink it too much.

note: long · dense, every dimension present
transcript: Took my Concerta at 8 after about six hours of broken sleep. Slow start, foggy until the coffee and the meds kicked in together around 9:30. Then a really solid focused stretch, locked in on the proposal for three hours straight. Skipped lunch which I always regret, got the dry mouth thing again. Crashed mid-afternoon, felt low and snappy, but a walk helped and I ended the day feeling okay, quietly satisfied I'd actually shipped the thing.

note: long · frustrated venting, low mood
transcript: Everything felt like too much today. The smallest tasks took enormous effort, I snapped at my partner over nothing, and I keep feeling like I'm falling behind on every single front. I don't even know what's wrong exactly, just a heavy grey feeling that wouldn't lift no matter what I tried.

note: negation · hedged, better than expected
transcript: Honestly not as bad as I expected. I braced for a terrible day but it turned out fine, pretty steady actually.

note: negation · double negative mood
transcript: I didn't feel terrible today, which for me counts as a win. Not great, not bad, just kind of neutral and getting on with things.

note: negation · energy, contrary to expectation
transcript: Slept badly so I expected to be wiped out, but surprisingly I wasn't tired at all. Had decent energy right through to the evening.

note: negation · strong focus negative
transcript: I really had no focus whatsoever today. Couldn't hold a single thought long enough to act on it.

note: dense · mood + energy + focus packed in
transcript: Felt good, full of energy, and razor sharp all morning. One of those rare days where everything lines up and the brain just cooperates.

note: fragment · terse negative
transcript: Exhausted. Couldn't focus on anything. Low.

note: fragment · terse positive
transcript: Good day. Slept well, got loads done, felt sharp.

note: very short · single sentence low
transcript: Drained and flat from the moment I woke up.

note: anxiety · acute, avoidance
transcript: I'm panicking about the deadline and I keep avoiding the email thread. Spent the evening doomscrolling instead of dealing with it.

note: social · post-interaction exhaustion
transcript: Back to back meetings and a long lunch with people left me completely drained. I'm an empty shell tonight, just need silence.

note: quiet win · understated positive
transcript: Nothing dramatic, but I cleared the small admin tasks I'd been putting off for weeks and felt quietly content about it. Grateful for a calm evening.

note: activity · exercise lift
transcript: Forced myself to the gym even though I didn't want to, and afterwards felt amazing, clear-headed and energised for the rest of the day.

note: voice import · 2026-06-18_14-30_demo-session.md
transcript: So I'm thinking about the architecture for the new feature set. The main problem we're trying to solve is improving the test coverage for the AppCore Swift Package. Right now we've got the TDD loop set up on the Linux VM, which is working pretty well with swift test. The key thing is keeping the logic testable and separated from the iOS UI layer. That's why we're using the AppCore package — it's basically a pure Swift library that doesn't have any UIKit dependencies. I was looking at some patterns for organizing the test structure. We could do it by feature or by layer. I think by feature makes more sense because it keeps the tests closer to the actual implementation. Another thing to consider is the CI/CD pipeline. We need to make sure tests run automatically on every push. With the GCP VM setup, we can hook that into GitHub Actions pretty cleanly. One more thing — I should probably set up a memory system for tracking all the architectural decisions we're making. Something like an ADR folder would be helpful for documenting why we chose certain patterns over others.

note: grounded · med tolerance, 'doesn't hit the same' (adultingadhd.substack)
transcript: I've been on the same Elvanse dose for about six months and honestly it doesn't hit the same as it used to. The early days I felt like a completely different person, switched on, present. Now it's more like I'm just getting to baseline. I mentioned it to my psychiatrist and she said we could try bumping the dose but I'm not sure I want to chase that feeling forever.

note: grounded · executive function spoons exhausted (adhdos.substack)
transcript: I used all my executive function spoons just getting out of the door this morning. By the time I sat down at my desk I was already done. Showering, getting dressed, making breakfast — each one felt like a project. Couldn't face the actual work after that. The bar for a good day is just too high when the morning costs this much.

note: grounded · 'bad brain day' language, shutdown (chaospalace.substack)
transcript: Bad brain day. That's all I can really say about it. Memory was a huge problem — I couldn't retain anything I read, kept losing track of what I was doing mid-sentence. The kind of day where you spend twenty minutes looking for your keys and they're in your hand.

note: grounded · stimulant body buzz, felt it kicking in (nikema.substack)
transcript: Took my Ritalin at eight and about an hour later I felt that familiar buzz in my body. Not unpleasant, just that shift where the static in my head goes quiet. The morning routine actually happened in the right order for once. I noticed I was walking with intention instead of just drifting from room to room.

note: grounded · 'brain refuses to do the most basic shit' (adhdmademedoit.substack)
transcript: My brain just refused to do the most basic shit today. I sat on the couch for two hours meaning to reply to one email. One email. Instead I scrolled, made tea I didn't drink, started three different things, and ended up doing nothing. The worst part is I could see myself doing it and I still couldn't stop.

note: grounded · officially logging out, setting a limit (noenthuda.substack)
transcript: I officially logged out of work mode at four today and refused to check Slack after that. It sounds small but for me it's huge — I usually work-creep into the evening and then wonder why I'm wired and can't sleep. The rest of the afternoon was scattered but at least it was mine.

note: grounded · surprise productive burst, didn't see it coming (noenthuda.substack)
transcript: Had an unexpected productive burst this afternoon. I wasn't planning to work, just going to tidy up a bit. Then something clicked and I ended up finishing the whole thing in one go. I don't know what the difference was, honestly. The brain is just unpredictable sometimes.

note: grounded · restless but exhausted paradox (toolatesmart.substack)
transcript: Classic fidgety-but-tired situation today. Couldn't sit still, kept getting up, couldn't focus on anything for more than five minutes. But also completely exhausted, like my body was running on empty. Unable to focus, mood all over the place. It's one of the worst combinations — restless and depleted at the same time.

note: grounded · clarity day, walking into rooms knowing why (latetomyownparty.substack)
transcript: Something is different today. I walk into rooms and I know why I'm there. That sounds like nothing but it's everything. Usually I get up to do something and by the time I've taken three steps I've forgotten what it was. Today the thread stayed connected. Got through my whole list and still had energy.

note: grounded · new med first days, super productive (mindmate.org.uk)
transcript: First couple of days on the new dose and I feel super productive, which I know might just be the honeymoon period. Everything is sharper, quicker. I'm trying not to get too attached to this feeling because I know the adjustment might smooth out. But right now it's good.

note: grounded · racing thoughts at night, can't wind down (chaospalace.substack / adhdos.substack)
transcript: Got into bed at a reasonable time for once and then my brain just took off. Racing through tomorrow's to-do list, then some conversation from three weeks ago, then what I should have said in the meeting. By 1am I gave up and read for a bit. Took ages to come back down. Three or four hours of sleep, rough.

note: grounded · memory failures, cognitive fog (chaospalace.substack)
transcript: Memory is a huge problem today. Walked into the kitchen, no idea why. Looked at my calendar and couldn't remember booking half the things on it. Had a conversation with my manager and by the time I sat back down I'd lost the details of what we decided. Wrote it all down but it still feels like it's going through sand.

note: grounded · time blindness, hours disappeared unaccounted (adultingadhd.substack)
transcript: I looked at the clock and it was somehow 3pm. I genuinely don't know where the morning went. I wasn't sleeping, I wasn't hyperfocused on anything useful, time just… slipped. It's a horrible feeling, like losing hours of your life and having nothing to show for it.

note: grounded · sudden irritability, disproportionate reaction (adhdos.substack)
transcript: Got disproportionately upset about something completely minor this afternoon. A small inconvenience and I went from zero to really irritable in about thirty seconds. I knew in the moment it was too big a reaction but I couldn't dial it back. The emotional part of my brain just does what it wants sometimes. Calmed down an hour later and felt stupid about it.

note: grounded · RSD, critical feedback landed badly (adhdos.substack / adultingadhd)
transcript: Got some critical feedback at work today that was completely fair and reasonable but it hit me like a wall. Spent the rest of the afternoon in a spiral, questioning everything. Logically I know it's not the end of the world. But the feeling of being rejected or criticised just floods everything. Hard day.

note: grounded · hyperfocus trap, locked in on irrelevant task (adultingadhd.substack)
transcript: Hyperfocused on completely the wrong thing for three hours. Went down a rabbit hole reorganising my filing system when I had an actual deadline. The focus was perfect — just aimed at entirely the wrong target. Snapped out of it at 2pm feeling equally satisfied and horrified.

note: grounded · avoidance spiral, phone instead of task (adhdmademedoit.substack)
transcript: I needed to make one phone call. That's all. Instead I spent two hours on my phone doing absolutely nothing productive, just doomscrolling and refreshing things. I know it's avoidance. I know that making the call would take six minutes and I'd feel better. Still didn't do it. Tomorrow.

note: grounded · afternoon medication rebound, irritable + low (nikema.substack)
transcript: The Elvanse wore off around four and it was rough. Went from fine to flat in about forty minutes. The rebound irritability is real — I'm short with people, everything feels harder, motivation drops off a cliff. I've started scheduling difficult tasks for the morning now because the afternoon is basically written off.

note: grounded · full stimulant day arc: onset→peak→crash→rebound (nikema.substack / mindmate.org.uk)
transcript: Concerta 36 this morning. Kicked in about 9, I was sharp and quick all morning, really good stretch of focus. Peak was probably 11 to 1. Slowed down after lunch, which is normal. By 4 the crash was real — dry mouth, flat mood, low energy. Felt okay by 7 once it fully cleared. Solid day overall but the rebound window is a problem.

note: grounded · unexpected productive end to a scattered day (noenthuda.substack)
transcript: The whole day felt scattered and pointless. Kept starting things and putting them down. Then at about 5pm I sat down and just quietly knocked off the three things I'd been avoiding all week. No idea what changed. Maybe the pressure of the end of the day. I'll take it.

note: grounded · sensory sensitivity, overstimulated (adhdos.substack)
transcript: Everything felt too loud today. The office was the usual noise level but it was grating in a way it doesn't always. Couldn't filter it. Headphones on, still couldn't settle. Made a few mistakes because my brain was just too overloaded to hold the details. Took the afternoon off early.

note: grounded · morning routine actually worked, detail-forward (nikema.substack)
transcript: Took my meds at seven with food like I'm supposed to. Shower actually happened before I looked at my phone. Made coffee. Left the house without forgetting anything. I know that sounds like the bare minimum but it was a proper morning routine and it set the whole day up well.

note: grounded · post-work crash, couch, phone, nothing (adhdmademedoit.substack)
transcript: Got home and immediately crashed onto the couch. All I wanted to do was lay there and scroll. Didn't cook, didn't shower, didn't do the one errand I'd been putting off all week. Just flat. Sometimes after a big cognitive day there's nothing left and you just have to let the couch have you.

note: grounded · structure collapsed without external scaffolding (adultingadhd.substack)
transcript: Weekends are hard. No schedule, no external structure, and everything just kind of collapses. Woke up at 10, spent three hours in a fog not doing anything. By the time I had enough momentum to do something it was already late afternoon. I need external structure more than I realise until it's gone.

note: grounded · compensatory hypervigilance, double-checking (adhdos.substack)
transcript: Spent a lot of today double-checking everything because my working memory is just not to be trusted. Re-read emails before sending, wrote things down twice, set three alarms for the same meeting. It's exhausting in a different way than a bad focus day — it's the cognitive load of managing the gaps.

note: med · Adderall, calm productive clarity, all-day effect (additudemag.com)
transcript: The Adderall 20mg today was just right. Not wired, not flat — calm in a way I rarely feel. I could actually stay on one thing. My head wasn't bouncing around. Got through the big report in one sitting which I genuinely did not think was possible. Felt like myself, but a version of myself that's actually functioning.

note: med · Elvanse onset window, step by step (additudemag.com)
transcript: Took my Elvanse 50mg at 7:30 with breakfast. By 8:15 I could feel something settling — not dramatic, just the background static getting quieter. Properly kicked in around 9. Sharp for the whole morning. The concentration window is real and I'm trying to use it better instead of wasting it on emails.

note: med · Concerta slow-release wearing off, IR top-up (additudemag.com reviews)
transcript: Concerta 36mg this morning and it improves my concentration immeasurably but it doesn't last long enough for me. Wore off around 2pm, which is early. I had a 4pm call that went badly because I was already crashed. I need to talk to the doctor about either a higher dose or adding a short-acting IR in the afternoon.

note: med · Ritalin timing error, sleep anxiety (additudemag.com)
transcript: Took my Ritalin at 11 because I forgot the morning dose. Spent the whole afternoon focused but also anxious about whether it would ruin my sleep. Lay there at midnight, mind racing, and I was right to worry. About four hours of sleep. I really can't take it after nine at the latest.

note: med · Vyvanse appetite suppression, forgot to eat (additudemag.com)
transcript: Vyvanse 40mg and I completely forgot to eat all day. Looked up at 6:30pm and realised I'd had nothing since the protein bar at breakfast. Headache, slightly shaky, cranky. The focus was good but running on empty isn't sustainable. Need to set alarms for meals on Vyvanse days.

note: med · planned drug holiday weekend, unmedicated experience (additudemag.com)
transcript: Drug holiday today, no Concerta. My psychiatrist suggested trying a weekend off every month. By 10am I'd already lost my keys, forgotten what I was doing twice, and abandoned two tasks. But I also ate a full meal and my heart rate felt calmer. It's a trade-off. I understand now why people say it's not just 'willpower' without the meds.

note: med · dose increase adjustment, first week effects (additudemag.com)
transcript: First week on Elvanse 60mg up from 50. More alert but also more irritable, which I didn't expect. Focus is sharper than before but there's an edge to it. Sleep has been harder. I think it needs time to settle. Going to give it two more weeks before deciding if this dose is right.

note: med · first stimulant ever, day one (additudemag.com 'eureka' account)
transcript: Today was the first day I ever took a stimulant medication. I did not know my brain could feel like this. The chaos got quieter. I actually sat at my desk and worked for two hours without getting up or checking my phone. I cried a little bit in the afternoon not from sadness but from the realisation that this is what other people's brains feel like all the time.

note: med · caffeine stacked on stimulant, jittery (additudemag.com)
transcript: Made the mistake of having a double coffee on top of my Concerta this morning. By 9:30 I was jittery, hands a bit shaky, heart going faster than I liked. Couldn't settle, couldn't channel the energy into anything useful. Classic overcaffeination on top of a stimulant. Lesson: stick to one coffee or skip it entirely on med days.

note: med · experiment with taking meds earlier (additudemag.com)
transcript: Tried taking my Elvanse at 6:30am instead of 7:30 to see if I could get a better morning. It did kick in faster but I was also tired and wired at the same time by 8am which felt strange. The afternoon coverage was better though. I think I'll experiment for another week before deciding. Medication management is its own full-time job.

note: med · tolerance creeping up, 'can't feel it at all' (additudemag.com review 'Andrew1')
transcript: Been on this Ritalin dose for about six months and I genuinely can't feel it working anymore. Not a crash, just... nothing. After six months of it being noticeable I can't tell when it's kicked in. I've read this is normal but it's disheartening. Mentioned it to my GP and we're going to try switching formulations before jumping the dose.

note: med · brand to generic switch, felt different (additudemag.com)
transcript: Pharmacy switched me to generic methylphenidate this month. It should be identical but something feels different. The onset is less smooth, there's more of an edge to it, and the comedown is harder. I know the active ingredient is the same on paper but in practice it's not quite right. Going to ask for the brand name back.

note: med · rebound anxiety as meds clear, 5pm (additudemag.com)
transcript: The meds wore off around five and instead of just going flat like usual, I got a wave of anxiety. Not about anything specific, just a free-floating dread. Heart a bit fast, couldn't sit still, low-grade panic. Lasted about an hour and then lifted. The rebound isn't always low mood — sometimes it's anxiety and it catches me off guard every time.

note: med · stimulant dehydration headache (additudemag.com)
transcript: Headache from late morning that I'm pretty sure is from not drinking enough water. Stimulants make me forget I'm thirsty and then I get these slow grinding headaches by 11am. Took some ibuprofen and drank a litre of water and it helped a bit but I was basically useless until 2pm. Need to put a water bottle in front of my face every morning.

note: med · late Elvanse → insomnia until 3am (additudemag.com)
transcript: Took my Elvanse at noon because I had a late start. Bad idea. By 11pm I was still completely awake, mind moving fast, couldn't even doze off. Clock said 1am, then 2am, then 3am. Exhausted but lit up. The half-life on Elvanse is long and I keep forgetting that. The sleep deprivation the next day absolutely wrecked any benefit from the dose.

note: med · appetite gone, forcing food deliberately (additudemag.com)
transcript: Set a phone alarm for 1pm just to make myself eat something. Without it I'd skip lunch entirely on Vyvanse — I just don't feel hunger. Forced down half a sandwich. By 7pm when it wore off I was ravenous and ate too much too fast. Still figuring out how to eat properly on medication days.

note: med · Wellbutrin added, smoother comedown (additudemag.com)
transcript: Two weeks since adding Wellbutrin to the Concerta. The late afternoon crash is noticeably softer. I don't hit the wall as hard around 4pm. Mood is more stable across the day, less of that flat pit feeling when the stimulant wears off. Not perfect but a genuine improvement. First medication change that's made a positive difference in months.

note: med · stimulant working cognitively but emotional flatness (additudemag.com)
transcript: The Elvanse is doing its job — I'm focused, productive, getting things done. But I feel a bit emotionally flat. Not sad, just... muted. Like the volume on everything's been turned down a notch. My partner mentioned I seem quieter. I don't know if this is the medication or just a coincidence. Going to track it for a few more weeks.

note: med · all three signals positive, rare best-case day (additudemag.com)
transcript: Concerta day that just worked. Mood was genuinely good from the start. Energy was steady without being wired. Focus was where I needed it. Got through a full workday without derailing, had a real conversation with my partner in the evening, went to bed at a reasonable hour. These days remind me what the medication is supposed to do.

note: med · adjusting to new medication, week one uncertainty (additudemag.com)
transcript: First week on Atomoxetine after being on stimulants. Completely different. It's not a switch you flip, it's supposed to build up over weeks. I don't notice anything yet except for feeling slightly nauseated in the mornings. I'm told to give it a month. That's a long time to wait while still struggling. Trying to be patient.

note: exec · task initiation gap, knowing vs starting (additudemag.com / psychologytoday.com)
transcript: I knew exactly what I needed to do. The task was right there. I had the document open. And I sat there for two hours not starting it. It's not laziness — I wanted to do it, I knew I should, I felt the pressure of the deadline. The gap between knowing and starting is something I can't explain to people who don't have this. It's like the signal isn't getting through.

note: exec · doom pile, looked at it and retreated (lifeskillsadvocate.com)
transcript: Looked at the pile on my desk today and felt physically sick. It's not just clutter — it's every pending decision I haven't been able to make, every item that needs to go somewhere but requires a chain of micro-decisions I can't face. I know what a doom pile is now. Backed away and did something easier instead. The pile grows.

note: exec · body doubling on video call, actually got things done (flow.club)
transcript: Did a coworking video call with a friend today — we both just sat there working in silence on our own stuff. I got more done in two hours than I had in the previous two days combined. The presence of another person was enough. I don't fully understand it but I'm not questioning it. Body doubling is real and I'm booking more of these.

note: exec · Pomodoro timer worked, time boundary helped (lifeskillsadvocate.com)
transcript: Tried the 25-minute Pomodoro thing today and it actually helped. Knowing I only had to stay on task for 25 minutes made it less overwhelming to start. The timer also kept time blindness in check — I could feel the shape of the work period instead of drifting. Managed five rounds which is probably my best focused output in weeks.

note: exec · task switching overhead, each switch expensive (helloklarity.com)
transcript: Every time I had to switch tasks today I felt like I was paying a toll. Twenty minutes to get back into something properly after being pulled away. Had four interruptions and never really got deep into anything. The context switching cost is real — I read that it's worse for ADHD brains and today I believe it.

note: exec · forgot thought mid-sentence, working memory gap (additudemag.com)
transcript: Lost my train of thought mid-sentence in a meeting today. Just gone. I was in the middle of making a point and the next word disappeared and I couldn't find it. Had to say 'sorry I lost it' and that was that. It's embarrassing in a way that's hard to shake. My working memory is genuinely unreliable and I hate it.

note: exec · hyperfocus on code, 7 hours, forgot everything (additudemag.com / psychologytoday.com)
transcript: Got into the code around 10am and didn't look up until 5. Seven hours. I know the specific problem I was solving isn't even the most important thing but it had me completely locked in — I didn't eat, didn't drink, missed a call. When I'm in it, 'ADHD is like living five minutes in the future. When I hyperfocus the world doesn't exist.' That's the most accurate description I've seen.

note: exec · reading impossible, words not retaining (additudemag.com)
transcript: Tried to read a report this morning and I got through the first paragraph three times without retaining any of it. The words just bounced off. Kept reading the same sentence over and over, finished the paragraph, and had no idea what it said. Reading is supposed to be easy for me. Brain fog days make it feel like a foreign language.

note: exec · executive function depleted by afternoon, can't choose (additudemag.com)
transcript: By 3pm I couldn't make a single decision. Asked what I wanted for dinner and just couldn't answer. Two options and I froze. All the small decision-making throughout the day had completely depleted whatever cognitive resource handles that. Decision fatigue hits me harder than most people and the afternoon is when it becomes a real problem.

note: exec · locked in on irrelevant thing again, different day (additudemag.com)
transcript: Somehow spent 90 minutes making a colour-coded spreadsheet for something that did not need a colour-coded spreadsheet. It started as a tiny tangent and then I just couldn't stop. The focus was excellent, the output was real, it was just completely misallocated. A race car brain with bicycle brakes — I can go, I just can't steer.

note: exec · list didn't help initiation, still couldn't start (additudemag.com)
transcript: Made a to-do list first thing. Priority order, time estimates, everything. Still couldn't start the top item. The list wasn't the problem. Knowing what to do was never the problem. It's the initiation that breaks down and a list doesn't fix that. Spent 45 minutes on the list and then avoided everything on it.

note: exec · calendar set, still forgot (additudemag.com)
transcript: I put the meeting in the calendar. The reminder went off. I saw it. And then 20 minutes later I was doing something else and missed the meeting entirely. I'm not sure how to explain this to people. The information reached me, I processed it, and then it just didn't translate into action. This is not how my brain is supposed to work and I don't know how to fix it.

note: exec · single completed task, reframing success (additudemag.com)
transcript: I did one thing today. One actual completed task from start to finish. Normally I'd catastrophise about everything else I didn't do. But today I'm choosing to count this. Getting started is the hardest part and I started and finished something. That's not nothing.

note: exec · sensory filtering breakdown, background unbearable (psychologytoday.com)
transcript: Couldn't filter the background noise today. Someone's music two desks over, the HVAC, people's footsteps — all carrying equal weight in my brain. Can't distinguish what to pay attention to. I've read that this is an ADHD thing — information all arrives at the same volume with no prioritisation. Put my headphones in but the headphones were also just adding another layer.

note: exec · 90-minute writing flow, unexpected (psychologytoday.com)
transcript: New ideas emerging like shooting stars — that's actually what it felt like this afternoon. Got into a writing flow from about 2 to 3:30 that I wasn't expecting. Ninety minutes of things just coming out. Didn't force it, just started and it arrived. I don't know what creates these conditions but when it happens I try not to question it.

note: exec · paralysis then surprise output, deadline pressure (additudemag.com)
transcript: Stuck for four hours doing absolutely nothing on the project. Then at 4pm, with the deadline at 5, something unlocked. I wrote more in fifty minutes than I had all week. This is the most dysfunctional version of productivity I can imagine but it's how my brain works with deadlines. 'Now and not now' — the deadline made it NOW.

note: exec · room full of incomplete tasks, doom spiral (lifeskillsadvocate.com)
transcript: Looked around the flat tonight and counted: laundry half folded, dishes in the drying rack but not put away, one bill paid out of three, a book with a bookmark at page 12 from two weeks ago. Everything half done. It's not laziness — I genuinely start things and then the next step requires a decision or a context switch and it just doesn't happen.

note: exec · tangent research rabbit hole (additudemag.com)
transcript: Went to look one thing up. Three hours later I had seventeen browser tabs open, knew a lot about something I didn't need to know about, and had done none of the actual work. My brain treats every interesting new piece of information as equally urgent. The rabbit hole was fascinating and completely useless. Closed all the tabs and felt the loss.

note: exec · mental busyness, nothing produced (additudemag.com / psychologytoday.com)
transcript: My brain was going all day. So much happening up there — ideas, half-thoughts, things I should do, things I regret, plans, worries. The noise was constant. But none of it translated into any actual output. Exhausted at the end of the day having done almost nothing visible. Like running on a hamster wheel, nonstop at full speed, and getting nowhere.

note: exec · completed three tasks start to finish (additudemag.com)
transcript: Managed three tasks today without a single interruption to something else. Finished each one before starting the next. This doesn't sound like an achievement but for me it actually is. Something about the day — maybe the sleep, maybe the timing of the meds — made the transitions manageable. Wish I knew the exact combination so I could replicate it.

note: mood · RSD from unreplied message, anxiety spiral (PMC/pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12822938)
transcript: Sent a message to a friend two days ago and they still haven't replied. I know they're probably just busy. I know it doesn't mean anything. But there's this feeling like 'a chair has been taken out from beneath me' and I can't reason myself out of it. Spent way too much time checking if they'd seen it. This is rejection sensitivity and I hate how real it feels.

note: mood · RSD from manager's tone, didn't say anything explicit (PMC/pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12822938)
transcript: My manager's tone in the standup today felt off. Nothing explicit, no criticism. Just a slight flatness and I immediately reflexively heard it as 'you're a bad person' and went into a spiral. Spent the next hour not working, just sitting with a burning feeling in my chest, going over everything I'd done wrong recently. By afternoon I'd talked myself down. But those hours were gone.

note: mood · small inconvenience → disproportionate response (additudemag.com)
transcript: Something tiny happened — the coffee machine was out of milk — and I felt completely overwhelmed by it. Not the milk. The milk was just the thing that broke through. Everything that had been building all week flooded in at once. I went and sat in the bathroom for five minutes. Embarrassing. I could see it happening and I felt helpless to stop it.

note: mood · mood dropped at 3pm, no reason (additudemag.com)
transcript: Mood just dropped at three. Nothing happened. Good morning, normal lunch, and then something shifted and I went flat. Everything felt effortful and pointless for about two hours. Picked up a bit by evening. I've started noticing these 3pm lows are almost clockwork some weeks. Don't know if it's the meds, blood sugar, circadian something, or just ADHD. Unsettling when there's no cause.

note: mood · chronic low-grade irritability, no specific cause (additudemag.com)
transcript: Not a bad day exactly. But there's been this undercurrent of irritability all day. I'm tense. A colleague asked me something routine and I had to really work to not snap at them. I'm always tense. I can never fully relax. People who don't have ADHD don't have this constant background noise of agitation and I genuinely don't know what that would feel like.

note: mood · cried at video, disproportionate (additudemag.com / PMC)
transcript: Cried watching a completely normal video at lunch. Not a sad one — it was about dogs. But something in it hit and I couldn't stop it. The emotional response in my brain doesn't match the stimulus. I'm fine, genuinely, but the emotional regulation is just not where it should be. These things don't embarrass me as much as they used to. It's just how I'm wired.

note: mood · high energy excellent mood, rare day (additudemag.com)
transcript: One of those rare days where mood and energy and focus all aligned. Felt genuinely good — like good in a way that's hard to describe because it's so infrequent. Ideas were coming fast, everything felt achievable, even the mundane tasks were fine. I know better than to set myself up for it happening tomorrow. But today was real and I'm grateful for it.

note: mood · comparing output to others, shame cycle (additudemag.com)
transcript: Made the mistake of comparing my output to a colleague's today. They finished three projects this week that I should have done. The shame spiral started quietly and then I was in it fully — inadequate, bad at my job, everyone can see it. I know intellectually this isn't a fair comparison. But the emotional part doesn't care about the intellectual part.

note: mood · finished backlogged task, quiet pride (latetomyownparty.substack.com)
transcript: I paid the bill I'd been putting off for six weeks. It took seven minutes. I felt proud enough to tell my partner about it, which made me feel slightly ridiculous, but this is what the medication gives me — the ability to do the thing that needs doing instead of avoiding it. Small wins aren't small when your baseline is avoidance.

note: mood · too many inputs, system shut down (additudemag.com)
transcript: The inbox, the to-do list, the unread messages, the thing I said I'd do last week — all of it arrived at once this morning and I just shut down. Pure desire to want to take on everything and then I ended up doing nothing. The overwhelm is real. When everything is equally urgent nothing can be prioritised and the brain gives up.

note: mood · catastrophising about upcoming event (additudemag.com)
transcript: The performance review is in two weeks and I've been catastrophising about it for days. My brain has already played out every possible bad outcome in detail. I know this is anxiety amplified by the ADHD nervous system, I know it probably won't be as bad as I'm imagining. But putting everything off 'til the last minute has wrecked a big chunk of my life and I'm scared it's going to catch up with me again.

note: mood · anhedonia, flat interest in everything (additudemag.com)
transcript: Nothing is interesting today. Usually there's something — a task I'm looking forward to, something I want to listen to, food I'm excited about. Today everything is equally meh. Not sad exactly, just flat. The interest-based nervous system apparently needs interest to function and today there is none. I went through the motions and that was it.

note: mood · annoyed all day, still got through it (additudemag.com)
transcript: Was irritated basically from the minute I woke up. Nothing in particular, everything in general. Still got through the work day. Made food. Didn't cancel anything. Sometimes you're frustrated and functional and that just has to count. Feeling good is not always a prerequisite for getting things done.

note: mood · unexpected calm, feels foreign (additudemag.com)
transcript: Felt genuinely settled today, which almost never happens. Not medicated-flat, actually calm. No background static. Not bracing for anything. I almost didn't know what to do with it. Kept waiting for the other shoe to drop. Managed a quiet productive afternoon and went to bed without the usual late-night brain loop. Want to understand what made today different.

note: mood · med rebound + underlying low, double dip (additudemag.com)
transcript: Meds wore off around 4:30 and instead of the usual flat, the flatness went all the way to genuinely low. Like the rebound hit on top of a mood that was already fragile. Ended up in a bad place emotionally for the evening — not crisis, just heavy. The interaction between stimulant rebound and whatever's happening with my mood baseline is something I need to talk to my doctor about.

note: sleep · delayed sleep phase, 2am is natural bedtime (additudemag.com)
transcript: Fell asleep at 2am again. I wasn't even trying to stay up — I was in bed by eleven, phone down, lights off. Just couldn't fall asleep. My sleep phase is shifted and has been my whole life. 2am feels natural in a way that 11pm never does. The problem is the world still needs me at 8am.

note: sleep · mind wouldn't stop, lying awake (psychologytoday.com / additudemag.com)
transcript: Can't turn my brain and body off to go to sleep. That's exactly what it is. Lay there for ninety minutes with my thoughts going — the meeting, the email I should have sent differently, something someone said a month ago. Like having 59 televisions blaring. Medication turns off 58 of them during the day. But at night they're all back on.

note: sleep · long sleep, still wrecked (additudemag.com)
transcript: Slept 11 hours last night. Finally a full sleep. Woke up and still felt exhausted, which is somehow more demoralising than feeling tired after bad sleep. At least then there's a cause. 11 hours and I still couldn't get going before noon. Not sure if it's sleep quality or something else but I can't keep using sleep as the explanation for feeling terrible.

note: sleep · melatonin 0.5mg worked, 7 hours (additudemag.com)
transcript: Tried 0.5mg melatonin at nine last night — much lower than the 5mg I was taking before. Something clicked. Fell asleep by 10:30 which is unheard of for me. Seven solid hours. Woke up before the alarm feeling actually rested. I've been taking too high a dose of melatonin apparently, which can make sleep worse. The low dose seems to be the answer.

note: sleep · 8 hours → everything worked, direct causal chain (additudemag.com)
transcript: Eight hours, woke up naturally. The medication kicked in perfectly. Focus held all morning. Mood was level. I know sleep and ADHD symptoms are directly connected but it's one thing to know it and another to feel it this clearly. Good sleep is probably the biggest single lever I have on how my brain functions and I don't protect it nearly enough.

note: sleep · tried everything, still poor sleep (additudemag.com)
transcript: Tried the whole sleep hygiene list tonight. No screen after nine, dark room, cold, no caffeine after noon, reading before bed. Still didn't fall asleep until 1am. I think people without ADHD can follow a sleep routine and their brain cooperates. My brain doesn't cooperate. The routine isn't the problem. The problem is the delayed sleep phase and the racing thoughts.

note: sleep · 20-minute nap, completely changed the afternoon (additudemag.com)
transcript: Took a 20-minute nap at 2pm and it completely changed the afternoon. Went from grey and flat and useless to functional. I'd been resisting naps because they feel like giving up but this was just the right reset. Not groggy afterwards, just refreshed. I need to get over the guilt about napping and just treat it as a management tool.

note: sleep · Elvanse at 11am → awake until 3am (additudemag.com)
transcript: Took my Elvanse at eleven because it was a late start. Completely forgot about the half-life until I was lying wide awake at 2am. Still going at 3. The long duration of lisdexamfetamine is a feature during the day and a bug at night. I cannot keep doing this. It needs to be seven at the absolute latest, no matter how late I sleep in.

note: sleep · snooze marathon, couldn't get up (additudemag.com)
transcript: Hit snooze seven times. I'm not exaggerating. Each time I genuinely intended to get up, went back to sleep immediately, and then the alarm went off again. Eventually dragged myself up at 9:30 feeling guilty and groggy. The morning then felt like wading through molasses. Lost three hours of the day before it really started.

note: sleep · stress dream → early wake, anxious residue (additudemag.com)
transcript: Woke up at 5:30 from a stress dream about work — the specific content was incoherent but the feeling was all real. Couldn't get back to sleep. Lay there with the anxiety from the dream mixing with actual things I'm worried about. By the time the alarm went I'd been awake for two and a half hours and already felt defeated before the day began.

note: energy · couldn't get off couch, no drive whatsoever (additudemag.com)
transcript: I have nothing today. Zero. Meant to work from home and instead sat on the couch from 9 to 2 barely moving. Not depressed exactly — I don't feel sad. Just no energy, no motivation, no drive to do anything at all. Not the couch-as-rest kind of nothing. The couch-as-surrender kind. These days happen and I don't know what causes them.

note: energy · night owl activation, productive at wrong time (additudemag.com)
transcript: It's 10:30pm and I'm suddenly wide awake and full of ideas. This always happens. The energy and creativity that should be fuelling my 9-to-5 shows up reliably at the wrong time. I've gotten a lot done in the last hour. Tomorrow I'll be exhausted and the cycle continues. Night owl ADHD is a real scheduling nightmare.

note: energy · coffee did nothing, unusual (additudemag.com)
transcript: Two coffees today and I felt nothing. No energy lift, no focus boost, nothing. Some days caffeine helps bridge the gap and some days it's just a warm drink. Not sure if I've built up tolerance or if it's a bad brain chemistry day. Either way, I was dragging all morning with no chemical assistance working.

note: energy · unpredictable fluctuations, hour to hour (additudemag.com)
transcript: Energy was all over the place today. Alert at 9, crashed at 11, weirdly energetic at 1, dead by 3, came back at 5pm. No pattern I can make sense of. I can't plan around something this volatile. Scheduling important things for when I 'feel good' doesn't work when good and bad alternate every couple of hours.

note: energy · terrible morning, picked up significantly by noon (additudemag.com)
transcript: Morning was a write-off. Foggy, flat, couldn't get anything started. Then around noon something shifted and I was actually functional. Got more done between 12 and 3 than in the entire morning. I keep hoping I'll stop being a late-starter but I think this is just how I work. Need to stop scheduling important things before noon.

note: energy · 3pm crash every day this week, noticing the pattern (additudemag.com)
transcript: Third day in a row this week where I've hit a wall at exactly 3pm. Energy drops off, focus goes, everything becomes an effort. I think it's partly the medication timing and partly just circadian. I've started blocking that hour out and doing admin tasks during it since higher-order thinking is offline by then. The pattern is predictable at least.

note: energy · body ready, brain won't engage (additudemag.com)
transcript: Strange day — physically I feel fine, I went for a walk, I'm not tired in my body. But my brain is completely offline. Can't hold a thought, can't start a task. The physical energy and the cognitive availability just aren't connected today. I keep expecting one to help the other and it's not working.

note: energy · had it and allocated it correctly (additudemag.com)
transcript: Had decent energy today and actually used it on the right things. Got the hardest task done first thing, which I almost never manage. When the energy dipped in the afternoon I switched to easier admin. It sounds like basic time management but for me it requires constant awareness of what my brain can actually do right now. Good day.

note: social · dominated meeting, can't stop talking (additudemag.com)
transcript: I talked too much in the meeting again. I could feel it happening — interrupting, adding things that didn't need to be added, just filling space. The taxing feeling of guilt about talkativeness happens every time. I didn't let other people finish their sentences and I know that. Working on it but it's genuinely hard to override.

note: social · dissociated mid-conversation, missed content (additudemag.com / psychologytoday.com)
transcript: Zoned out in the middle of a conversation today. The person was still talking, I was looking at them, and I was completely elsewhere. Came back and had missed something important. Had to ask them to repeat it. I dread watching movies or having conversations sometimes because I know I'll just tune out and miss the most important parts. It's not disrespect. My attention just goes.

note: social · cancelled social plan, guilt spiral (additudemag.com)
transcript: Cancelled on a friend today. I'd been dreading it all week — not the friend, just the energy it would take. But the guilt after cancelling is almost worse than going would have been. I don't socialise much anymore and I keep shrinking my circle. I avoid talking to people as much as possible and then feel lonely. The social avoidance loop is hard to break.

note: social · went to event, performed, came home empty (additudemag.com)
transcript: Went to the dinner party even though I didn't want to. Performed being okay for four hours. Made conversation, laughed at the right moments, nobody knew how much effort it was. Came home and sat in silence for an hour just recovering. Social events are cognitively expensive in a way I can't always explain to people. I don't always say the wrong thing anymore. I just always say the right thing at enormous cost.

note: social · relationship friction from ADHD forgetting (additudemag.com)
transcript: Argument with my partner tonight about something I forgot for the second time. It was a reasonable thing to be upset about — I said I'd do it and I didn't and then I forgot I'd said I'd do it. From the outside I can completely see how that looks. From the inside the forgetting is not deliberate and the shame of it is real. This keeps happening. I need better systems and a better way to explain what's going on.

note: social · told a friend, they actually got it (additudemag.com)
transcript: Explained my ADHD to a close friend today, properly, not just 'oh I have ADHD haha.' I explained the RSD, the time blindness, the initiation problems, the way interrupting happens before I can stop it. They listened and said 'that explains so much.' It felt like being understood for the first time in a long time. I don't always have the energy to explain but when it lands it's worth it.

note: social · caught myself interrupting, trying to fix it (additudemag.com)
transcript: Caught myself interrupting someone twice in the same conversation. The second time I apologised in the moment. The impulse to speak arrives before the other person has finished and stopping it requires a delay that my brain doesn't naturally build in. I'm working on it — literally counting to three before I respond — but I've been working on it for years.

note: social · group work draining, solo work night and day (additudemag.com)
transcript: Had to do group work today and it was exhausting compared to working solo. Every input from someone else required me to re-orient, the conversation moved faster than I could follow, and I lost my own thread three times. Then afterwards I did thirty minutes solo and got more done than in the two-hour group session. My brain performs very differently alone.

note: social · knew I should message, couldn't make myself (PMC/pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12822938)
transcript: I should have messaged three different people today. I knew it, I had my phone in my hand, and I just didn't. Not because I don't want to talk to them. Something about initiating contact takes executive function I didn't have. I rarely reach out. People probably think I don't care and that's not it at all. The initiation problem applies to relationships too.

note: social · always the one who doesn't initiate (PMC/pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12822938)
transcript: I noticed today that every text thread in my phone is started by the other person. Every plan has been made by them. I almost never reach out first. It's not that I don't want to — I think about people all the time. But the gap between thinking about them and actually sending a message is huge. Keep friendship circles small and full of people who are patient with me. Grateful for them.

note: long · full day with meds + mood + energy + focus (all sources)
transcript: Took Concerta 36 at 8am. Slow start but by 9:30 I was in it. Really productive morning — finished two things that had been on the list for two weeks. Lunch was fine but the afternoon started dragging around 2. Dry mouth kicked in, which is the signal that the crash is coming. Pushed through the 3pm dip with a walk outside. Mood held okay all day, maybe a 6 out of 10. Not a great day but a functional one, which is genuinely all I ask most days.

note: long · medication reflection after three months, balanced assessment (additudemag.com)
transcript: Three months on Elvanse. Honest summary: it helps. The mornings are better, the initiation problems are less severe, I'm getting more done. But it's not a cure and I think I expected it to be. The emotional dysregulation is still there. The time blindness is still there. The crash in the late afternoon is a consistent problem. The sleep is worse than before I started. Overall it's positive but it's not the simple fix I wanted. I think I was hoping the medication would do the work and I'm slowly understanding that it just makes the work possible.

note: long · what a properly functioning day looks like (latetomyownparty.substack.com / additudemag.com)
transcript: Today was a good day and I'm going to write it down so I can remember what one looks like. Woke at seven, took my meds at 7:15 with breakfast. Coffee. Checked my calendar before my phone. Started work at 9. Focused until noon with two small breaks. Ate lunch actually sitting down. Afternoon was slower but I switched to easier tasks and got through them. Finished at 5. Did the thing I'd been putting off — just paid it, took three minutes, felt like a weight lifted. Made dinner. Talked to my partner. Went to bed at 11. Nothing spectacular. But everything connected. That's what a good day feels like.

note: long · rough start with partial recovery (additudemag.com)
transcript: Woke up wrong. Groggy, flat, irritable before anything had even happened. Took the meds and waited. Morning was a write-off — couldn't start anything, just existed on the couch feeling useless. By noon I'd had enough of feeling sorry for myself. Forced myself to do one small task. Then another. By 3pm I'd actually done something. Not the day I planned but not a total loss. Some days the recovery is enough.

note: long · weekend structure collapse, honest account (additudemag.com)
transcript: Saturday: woke at 10:30, no medication because I'm trying to take breaks. No structure, no schedule, the whole day just kind of dissolved. Meant to do the laundry, the grocery shop, call my mum. Did none of it. Spent most of the day on my phone feeling guilty about spending most of the day on my phone. Sunday the same. By Sunday night I was anxious about the week ahead, exhausted from doing nothing, and behind on everything I'd planned. I need structure even on weekends. External structure is not a crutch, it's actually how I function.

note: long · Monday restart after rough week, trying again (additudemag.com)
transcript: Okay. New week. Monday reset. Took my meds on time. Made coffee. Wrote down three things I actually need to do today — not everything, just three. This is the thing about ADHD that's exhausting: the amount of effort required to manage the management systems. But last week was rough and I'm not ready to give up on this week. Three things. Then we'll see.

note: long · deadline day, all resources deployed (additudemag.com)
transcript: Project deadline today at 5pm. Took my Concerta early, skipped the leisurely morning, just started. The urgency unlocked something — this is the now-not-now thing in reverse. Now that it's NOW the brain activates. Finished with twenty minutes to spare. Heart was going the whole time. Couldn't eat all day. Felt triumphant and completely hollow afterwards. This is not a sustainable way to work but it's the way my brain works under pressure. I've been running on urgency for years.

note: long · therapy day, talked through ADHD stuff (additudemag.com)
transcript: Therapy this morning. We talked about the shame I carry about productivity — how I reflexively hear any criticism as 'you're a bad person' and jump into defensive mode. I didn't realise how much of my anxiety is just shame that's been internalised for years. The therapist said that for late-diagnosed ADHD adults this is really common — decades of struggling without explanation creates a specific kind of self-blame. Hard session. Tired now. Probably important though.

note: long · doctor appointment, dose changed, first day (additudemag.com)
transcript: Psychiatrist appointment this morning. She bumped me from Elvanse 50 to 60mg. Different prescription, first dose this afternoon to try. By 3pm I could feel the difference — more energised than usual, which could be great or could be too much. Sleep felt off tonight. Slightly jittery around 4pm. First day of a new dose is always information-gathering. Trying to notice things without overconcluding.

note: long · vent about backlog, everything piling up (additudemag.com)
transcript: I don't know where to start because everything has piled up and all of it needs doing and I can't prioritise. The emails I haven't replied to. The bills. The health thing I keep saying I'll call about. The work stuff that's spilled into the following week. When everything is equally urgent I can't move on any of it. The overwhelm is total. I know intellectually there's a way through this. I can't access it right now.

note: long · traction after two rough weeks (additudemag.com / noenthuda.substack)
transcript: Something shifted today. Two weeks of basically nothing getting done and then this morning I got up, made coffee, sat down, and just started. Not because I solved whatever was wrong. I don't know what changed. But I got through a backlog item I'd been dreading, then another, then a third. By noon I'd done more than in the last two weeks combined. These breakthrough days after slumps are the strangest thing. I always wonder if I made it happen or if it just happened to me.

note: long · friday reflection, honest mixed assessment (additudemag.com)
transcript: End of week review. What went well: I took my medication consistently every morning, I didn't miss any deadlines, I made it to the gym once. What didn't: I avoided two difficult conversations, the doom pile grew, I cancelled plans again. Sleep was poor all week. Mood was 5 out of 10 average. It was a functional week but barely. I'm proud of the medication consistency. That's a win. Everything else is work in progress and that has to be okay.

note: long · voice note in car, unfiltered end of day (additudemag.com)
transcript: Recording this driving home so I don't lose it. Today was one of those days where the meds wore off at exactly the wrong time — I had a meeting at four and I was already crashing at three. Got through it but I was slower, less sharp, probably said a few things twice. The dry mouth was brutal. I need to figure out a better system for late afternoon meetings. Also I forgot to eat again. Also I'm out of milk. That's it, that's the whole day.

note: long · unmedicated morning, pre-dose state (additudemag.com)
transcript: Writing this before I take my meds this morning. Brain is doing its thing — already thinking about seventeen things, none of them the thing I need to think about. Can't quite hold a thought long enough to do anything with it. This is what it's like without the medication. Not dramatically bad, just perpetually scattered. Like a browser with 600 tabs all loading at once. Medication closes all but the three I actually need. Taking them now.

note: long · late night reflection, should be sleeping (additudemag.com)
transcript: It's 12:30am and I should be asleep. Instead I'm lying here doing a full review of everything that happened today, everything I didn't do, and everything I'm worried about for tomorrow. The ADHD brain has no natural 'off switch'. I can't turn it off to go to sleep at night. Melatonin is next to the bed. Going to try. Tomorrow I'll be tired and the whole cycle starts again.
